title: continuous-batcher: scheduler tuning for queueing fairness and starvation prevention with timeouts
author: Evan Brooks
description: Motivation: under high-mixed-load scenarios the continuous-batcher scheduler allowed large, long-running batches to dominate queue slots and KV cache resources which caused tail latency spikes and observed starvation of low-latency single-request traffic. This PR adds a set of scheduler tunings and safeguards: 1) per-priority queue aging (configurable weights) so older small requests gain scheduling priority over newly enqueued large batches, 2) max-wait timeouts with graceful fallback to a fast single-request path (configurable by model/route), 3) preemption heuristics that break oversize queued batches when latency SLOs are approaching, 4) fairness tokens per client/account to reduce variance in throughput allocation, 5) KV cache reservation adjustments to prevent large KV-consuming requests from evicting hot prefixes used by low-latency routes, and 6) new observability (metrics/tracing) and feature flags. The description below includes implemented changes, tests and rollout plan. Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked in ENG-4212 - [x] Scheduler core implementation with feature flag - [x] Unit tests for queue aging and timeouts - [x] Integration test in perf-canary - [x] E2E perf numbers collected and validated - [x] Add runtime knobs and documentation - [x] Rollout: staged on Dedicated then hosted with feature gate and KillSwitch

review_comments: Priya Kumar: Can we make aging_weights per-model overrideable rather than global? I'm worried large multi-tenant models need stricter defaults.
Evan Brooks (author): Good point — implemented per-model override with a sensible global default. Added note in docs and config. See commit f21a33e.
Jorge Martinez: The preemption path looks racy with concurrent batch assembly. We need a small critical section or CAS to avoid double-preempting the same batch.
Evan Brooks: Added a lightweight atomic flag on BatchDescriptor and moved the preemption decision into the queue_manager critical section. Added unit test to assert single preemption per-batch.
Lindsey Zhao: Observability looks good; can we also emit a sample trace linking preemption->eviction->timeout for postmortems?
Evan Brooks: Added trace spans and propagated request IDs through the preemption and KV eviction code paths. Perf overhead measured <1% in our canary.
Priya Kumar: CI showed a flaky test on first run (TestQueueAging) — fixed by using a deterministic clock in tests. Verified stable on rerun.
ci_checks: unit-tests: passed after rerun with deterministic clock
release_notes: continuous-batcher: improved fairness and reduced starvation for low-latency requests under mixed workloads
New knobs: continuous_batcher.aging_weights (global and per-model), continuous_batcher.max_wait_ms, continuous_batcher.preempt_threshold_pct
KV cache: hot-prefix reservation reduces eviction-induced latency regressions
Observability: metrics and traces for queue aging, preemptions and timeout fallbacks
merge_outcome: merged via squash-merge after approvals from Priya, Jorge and Lindsey. Merge includes the squash commit and release note entry. Feature behind default-off feature flag and staged rollout plan in docs.
test_plan: Unit tests added for deterministic queue aging, preemptions and timeout fallback. Integration test covers mixed request profile with small/large requests and validates no starvation. Perf canary run validates tail latency and throughput. Rollout: enable for 10% Dedicated pools for 48h, monitor continuous_batcher.queue_age and timeout_fallbacks, then widen to hosted with kill-switch ready.
perf_results: Microbench (simulated mixed load, 80% small single-turn, 20% long batched): small-request P99 latency reduced from 620ms -> 340ms (45% reduction)
Overall throughput impact: -2.3% under synthetic worst-case (acceptable tradeoff, configurable via preempt_threshold_pct)
KV cache hit-stability: hot-prefix eviction events down 78% in canary runs
Fairness metric (per-client throughput variance): variance reduced by 60% in mixed workload canary
notes: This PR is intentionally conservative: feature flag default is off and preemption only triggers when queue_age and model-level SLO projections indicate risk. Ops runbook added to docs/continuous-batcher.md. Follow-ups: evaluate ML-driven adaptive preemption thresholds (ENG-4250) and expose per-route telemetry in Redwood Console.
